## 🎓 Today's lesson
### Understanding Treasury Yields and Why 5% Matters
A **Treasury yield** is the annual return the US government pays to investors who lend it money by buying government bonds. When the **10-year US Treasury yield rises above 5%**, it sets the baseline borrowing cost for the entire economy. Banks price home mortgages, auto loans, and corporate credit cards off this rate. For everyday households, **higher Treasury yields mean more expensive car loans and mortgages**, making it harder to buy a home or refinance existing debt [[CNBC]](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/15/treasury-yields-deficit-national-debt-ai.html).
